headline_findings: A real ancestor lookup is possible: NPS CWSS bulk data exists as a public S3 mirror (Soldiers_Personz.tsv 1.19 GB, ~6.26M cards est., 42% Confederate in a 400 KB sample) - but its redistribution status needs written NPS confirmation.

OpenStreetMap contains 867 historic monument/memorial elements in the battlefield bbox; 177 of them are >60 m from any of the site's 512 monuments (38 named Confederate) and 20 site monuments have no OSM feature within 60 m; only 9 of the site's 512 monuments carry a src value.
Official Records Series I Vol 27 (3 IA items, 11.26 MB OCR, 3,578 pages) is public domain and is the best evidence base for the clock/time conflict (audit C4).
USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM (4 tiles, ~470-485 MB each) and LoC Warren/Bachelder maps make a real viewshed and an 1863-landscape layer possible (audit H8).

Rights-restricted sources must be link-out only: American Battlefield Trust (ToS forbids scraping and AI use), Ancestry family incl. Fold3 and Find a Grave (ToS forbids programmatic access and ML training), FamilySearch, ACHS, HMDB bulk (non-commercial only), Stone Sentinels, NHGIS.
NPS/Dyer battle-unit data lists 300 Union units and ZERO Confederate units for Gettysburg; the NPS public GIS has no monuments/fences/orchards/cannon layers.

rights_tiers.A: Public domain / CC0 / permissive with notice only: may be ingested, redistributed in derived shards, and embedded in retrieval index.
rights_tiers.B: Reusable with attribution and/or share-alike (CC BY, CC BY-SA, ODbL, MIT): ingest only into clearly separated files with per-record license + attribution; share-alike scope must be contained.
rights_tiers.C: Link-out only: rights-restricted or terms forbid scraping/AI use (ABT, Ancestry family, FamilySearch, ACHS, HMDB bulk, Stone Sentinels, NHGIS). Provide deep links, never fetch, store or embed content; never feed to any model.
rights_tiers.A-pending: Believed public but needs a written confirmation or a source-level check before publication (CWSS mirror).

crosswalk_design.purpose: One row per site unit so every source joins on the same key; enables 'who was in the 20th Maine?', OR-report tagging, monument-to-unit links, and DBpedia/Wikipedia links.

keys.site_id: regiment_id in data/oob/*.json, e.g. U-20ME, C-2SC, U-1ME-CAV (467 units incl. batteries per site UI; 487 dict rows counted when iterating the OOB files: 279 'U', 196 'C', 12 without id)
keys.cwss_unit_code: e.g. UME0020RI (Union Maine 20th Regiment Infantry), CVA0021RC (Confederate Virginia 21st Cavalry), UNY0071RI, UPA0028RI, UCT0002YAL (2nd Independent Battery CT Light Artillery)
keys.dbpedia_uri: nps_units.csv column, present for 1,163 of 7,011 units
keys.nps_oob_string: e.g. '19th Indiana Infantry- Col. Samuel J. Williams' from the NPS pages

algorithm: parse site_id with ^(U|C)-(\d+)([A-Z]{2})(?:-(CAV|ART|SS|SHARP))?$ -> side, ordinal, state
cwss_unit_code = side + STATE + zero_pad(ordinal, 4) + arm  where arm: infantry RI, cavalry RC, heavy artillery RAH; (verify arm code inventory from Regiments_Unitz.tsv REG_ARM/REG_TYPE)
